# Kondratiev waves

The proposal that capitalist economies move in long waves of forty to sixty years, each with a rising and a falling phase.

## Status

The statistical evidence is thin: there are too few waves to test anything. The idea survives as a frame for narrative rather than as a model. Its modern descendants tie each wave to a cluster of technologies, which is what [[Technology surges]] does with more care.

## Use in the essay

Useful as the oldest statement of the intuition that there is a clock slower than the business cycle.
